messages.author: 8f6ff46c9f9bbf52
messages.subject: Same fit indices when comparing a 3 first-order factors model to a 1 second-order factor model
parts:
Hello!
I'm trying to fit compare a model with 3 first order factors to a model with 1 second order factor. I'm getting the same fit for both models... Is it reasonable or something is missing? If this is correct how should I justify the choice of a model and not the other.

Here's my syntax:

###Modelo 3 factores###
modelo3<- 'SS =~ MaaP2 + MaaP5 + MaaP7 + MaaP13 + MaaP6 + MaaP8 + MaaP10 + MaaP14
SE =~ MaaP3 + MaaP11 + MaaP12 + MaaP15 
PA =~ MaaP1 + MaaP4 + MaaP9 + MaaP16'

fit3 <- cfa(modelo3, data=maap_total, estimator = "MLR")
summary(fit3, standardized=TRUE, fit.measures=TRUE)
reliability(fit3)


###Modelo 1 factor de segunda ordem###
modelo4<- 'SS =~ MaaP2 + MaaP5 + MaaP7 + MaaP13 + MaaP6 + MaaP8 + MaaP10 + MaaP14
SE =~ MaaP3 + MaaP11 + MaaP12 + MaaP15 
PA =~ MaaP1 + MaaP4 + MaaP9 + MaaP16
SR =~ SS + SE + PA'

fit4 <- cfa(modelo4, data=maap_total, estimator = "MLR")
summary(fit4, standardized=TRUE, fit.measures=TRUE)
reliability(fit4)

Any help would be much appreciated,
Thanks in advance!

messages.author: ad188126f9138663
messages.subject: Re: Same fit indices when comparing a 3 first-order factors model to a 1 second-order factor model
parts:
Teresa,
A factor model with three indicators is saturated.  Because you have three first-order factors, the second-order factor does not impose any further constraints.  So, the two models are statistically equivalent.

Your choice of model can be based on theory.  If the second-order factor has a good theoretical justification, then it offers a more informative way to model the data (but he correlated factor model is not wrong).  If there is reason to question the second-order factor model then there may be some other explanation for the factor correlations in the correlated factors model.  For example, the factors may bear direct causal relations to one another.  The correlated factors model is basically agnostic because it does not attempt to explain the factor correlations.

There is nothing lavaan specific to this issue.

Keith Markus
